 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Baltimore Ravens are acquiring veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .
 Brissett will add experience to a quarterback room that will be without starter Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley for the foreseeable future.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the trade is expected to be completed this coming weekend. That means the Ravens will not have Brissett for tomorrow night's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
 Schefter reported that the veteran QB is expected to start for Baltimore in its following game, against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 10's edition of "Monday Night Football."
 Baltimore is still set to start undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano. Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis will back him up, and both signed with the Ravens earlier this week.
 Baltimore signed Brissett for his experience. The Ravens' current quarterback room has no career passing touchdowns, while starting running back Derrick Henry has four.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Brissett finally signed with the Cardinals after holding out for a better contract. He led Arizona to a 3-5 record and has 1,719 passing yards, 10 touchdowns, and seven interceptions.
 The veteran quarterback was benched late in the third quarter of last week's game against the Dallas Cowboys. Arizona trailed 17-3, but Gardner Minshew led the Cardinals to a comeback win, beating the Cowboys in overtime.
 On Tuesday, it was announced that Minshew would start this week for Arizona against the Seattle Seahawks.
 While Ravens fans can get excited for the experience heading to their team, they will have to wait a week to see him in action. Baltimore's next game is tomorrow against the Jaguars, and the trade will not be completed in time for him to play.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement That means that Fagnano will lead the offense. Starting quarterback Lamar Jackson was added to injured reserve with a thumb injury , and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley was diagnosed with turf toe, which is expected to be season-ending.
 In relief last week, the rookie completed 10-of-21 passes for 91 yards and one interception. Fagnano also ran the ball three times for 3 yards.
